An AI model helped researchers find two decade-old bugs in the code behind up to 70% of the web. Then the exploit details leaked before the patch did.
 
This week on Security Intelligence, Nick Bradley, Don Cowan and Jim Guinn join host Patrick Austin to unpack three major cybersecurity stories.
 
First, PHP2Shell could let attackers take over vulnerable servers without logging in. But you can't patch what you can't find, and PHP is buried in more systems than most teams realize.
 
Then, Anthropic gives six outside evaluators employee-like access to test its AI models. Should frontier AI labs go further and let their competitors inspect their models?
 
Finally, attackers hijack 333 Tor exit relays, rerouting traffic to harvest credentials. The way in? A reused password. A reminder that even attackers aren't immune to bad security hygiene.

All that and more on Security Intelligence.

title: The PHP bug threatening the web. Plus, who's auditing AI?
